INSTRUCTIONS FOR CONTRIBUTORS AND CODING AGENTS
- Write the PR title and description in English, including headings, tables, checklists, and validation notes.
- Be factual and concise. This PR should make it easy to compare the original intent with the actual outcome.
- Record the plan before implementation in an issue, comment, or versioned document. Link the original version (prefer a permalink or commit SHA). Keep later revisions separate.
- If no plan existed before implementation, say so. Never present a retrospective plan as the original.
- Report what was completed, changed, skipped, or remains unverified. Explain meaningful deviations.
- List only agents, models, commands, test results, and approvals you can confirm. Use "Unknown" when model details are unavailable.
- Distinguish local checks from CI and human review. A passing check applies only to the revision it tested.
- Do not check boxes reserved for human reviewers or claim human approval on their behalf.
- Use "Not applicable — <reason>" where appropriate. Keep trivial changes brief.
-->

## Human Review (Reviewer Only)

<!-- The author/agent must leave this section untouched. Checkboxes are a review aid, NOT a substitute for GitHub's native PR reviews, required checks, or branch protection. -->

- [ ] I compared the original plan (or documented absence of one) with the delivered changes.
- [ ] I reviewed meaningful deviations, contributions, and the actual diff.
- [ ] I checked the evidence, tested revision, and known limitations.
- [ ] I considered risks, compatibility, dependencies, and rollback before approving.

- **Review reference:** <!-- Link to the actual GitHub review or review comment; reviewer fills in. -->
